chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrat, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked about a man while I was present, saying, 'What has prevented him from performing Hajj?' It was said, 'He has left trade and his effort has decreased.' He was reclining, then sat up straight, and said to them, 'Do not abandon trade, lest you become insignificant; trade, and Allah will bless you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on trade and its connection to religious duties like Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the common assumption that neglecting worldly affairs is a spiritual virtue, by identifying the man's delay in Hajj as a consequence of financial hardship caused by abandoning trade. He instructs his companions to maintain their commercial activities, promising that honest trade invites divine blessing (barakah), thereby establishing commerce as a legitimate and meritorious means of sustaining one's livelihood and religious obligations.
